name: Compounding Context
principle: What one run found is kept as a card that later runs reuse, so every run starts grounded in the person's material at little cost, reads only what is current, and can name where each piece came from.
state_description: A fresh corpus is grounded on its first task with no model call; a repeat task lands on the right sources before any search; the text a run sees is resolved from the current source; every card names its sources and who wrote it.
hints_of_measurement: Model calls and seconds spent assembling context per run, the rank of the right source for a task, stale sources served (none), and cards whose sources and writer are recorded (all).

name: One Ranked Context
principle: A run's context comes from one search over everything it may be grounded in, with one ranking and one budget, and every result says what kind of thing it is and where it lives.
state_description: A request that needs a file, a note and the solution it serves gets all three in one assembled view, ranked against each other under one budget, each labelled as a card or as a record of its kind, and each record read from its own file, never from a copy.
hints_of_measurement: On requests whose right answer mixes cards and records the expected items are in view; neither the card selection metric nor the specification selection metric drops; one model call or none per assembly.
